note: Re-judged 2026-11-03 (independent auditor, authored none of 2eebb4ac72). RFC 6286 Section 2.1: "The BGP Identifier is a 4-octet, unsigned, non-zero integer that should be unique within an AS. The value of the BGP Identifier for a BGP speaker is determined on startup and is the same for every local interface and every BGP peer." 2eebb4ac72 changed internal/component/bgp/reactor/config.go::parsePeerSettings only by adding checkASN4DisabledReachable (session_open_as.go), an RFC 6793 Section 4.1 refusal of asn4 disable with a four-octet remote AS; it reads DisableASN4, PeerAS, LocalAS and MigrationAS and never the identifier, and runs after the session router-id override is parsed, so it cannot preempt the zero refusal and does not fire on any tagged tree (none sets asn4 disable). The router-id path is unchanged: the global value is the default, session router-id overrides it per peer or group through parseRouterID, which still refuses 0 with the RFC 6286 Section 2.1 error. Tested 'non-zero integer': TestParsePeerFromTreeInvalid zero_router_id_rejected and TestRFC6286GlobalZeroRouterIDRejected assert the exact error for 0.0.0.0 on the per-peer and global leaves, and TestRFC6286NonZeroRouterIDAccepted plus the 0.0.0.1 half accept identifier 1 exactly; widening or removing the zero check reds them. All ran green 2026-11-03 under -race. Gap 'is determined on startup and is the same for every local interface and every BGP peer' stands: internal/component/bgp/reactor/reload_globals.go::applyGlobalsJournaled still applies a reloaded global router-id at runtime, and the per-peer override is the owner-approved deviation, not counted conformant. Tag polarity words read inverted (positive tags the rejecting cases), both directions present. Partial, zero whole-requirement credit.
